texts.preamble: Amit Solanki vs Sumit Solanki on 31 October, 2014 In The Court Of Ms. Geetanjli Goel, Po: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal2, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Suit No.124/14 Date of Institution: 20.09.2013 In The Matter Of: Amit Solanki S/o Shri Vijay Pal Solanki R/o H.No. Wz108, Dabri Village New Delhi110045. ...Petitioner Versus 1. Sumit Solanki S/o Shri Satpal Solanki R/o H.No. Wz155, Village Dabri New Delhi110045. 2. Kuldeep Solanki S/o Shri Jagbir Solanki R/o H.No. Wz155, Village Dabri New Delhi110045. 3. Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. Office At: 20221, 2nd Floor Mercantile House Kasturba Gandhi Marg New Delhi110001 . ...Respondents Suit No.124/14
texts.facts: 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on the night of 30/31st January, 2013 at about 3.00 a.m. the petitioner was coming back after attending a marriage function at Nangloi and the petitioner was accompanied by Shri Sumit Solanki who was driving the offending vehicle along with Shri Kuldeep Solanki and Shri Kaushal Kumar. It is averred that on the way at about 2/3 a.m. when the offending vehicle reached at Todarmal Road, Rattanpuri Chowk, the vehicle hit against a pole on the divider and the offending vehicle turned turtle and all the occupants received grievous injuries and became unconscious and the petitioner along with the other persons was removed to Lady Harding Hospital, New Delhi. The injured/petitioner was treated vide MLC No.38072/13. It is stated that in respect of Amit Solanki vs Sumit Solanki on 31 October, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119485754/ 1 the accident FIR No.17/2013 under Sections 279/338 IPC was registered against the respondent No.1 at PS Inder Puri. It is averred that due to the accident the petitioner/injured suffered tremendous mental agony, pain, suffering and loss of earnings. It is averred that the petitioner/injured spent approximately Rs.13,00,000/ (Rupees Thirteen Lacs Amit Solanki Vs. Sumit Solanki Page no. 2 of 23 only) on his treatment, special diet, transportation and attendant and the treatment was continuing. It is averred that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1 who was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner without caring for safety of the others and without following the traffic rules. It is averred that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence/rashness of the respondent No.1 who was driving the offending vehicle under the supervision of the respondent No.2 (owner of the offending vehicle) and the respondent No.3, who is the insurer of the offending vehicle, as such all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the injured/petitioner. It is stated that the petitioner is aged about 23 years and a student and he had completed the course of Software Engineering from Global Net India Institute, Bahadurgarh, Haryana. It is prayed that an amount of Rs.20,00,000/ be awarded as compensation in favour of the petitioner/injured and against the respondents jointly and severally. 3. Written submissions/ reasoned decision was filed on behalf of the respondent No.3 stating that the car No.DL4CAH6621 was duly insured with the respondent No.3 at the time of the alleged accident vide policy No. 1301722311002097 for the period from 20.9.2012 to 20.9.2013. It is averred that there is no document showing the period of treatment and the amount incurred by the injured on his treatment. An offer of Rs.32,254/ was made. Amit Solanki Vs. Sumit Solanki Page no. 3 of 23 4. Initially Detailed Accident Report was filed by the IO on 2.7.2013 and thereafter the claim petition was filed on 20.9.2013. On 30.1.2014 it was submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent No.3 that the reply filed to DAR be treated as the written statement to the claim petition. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 20.02.2014: 1. If so, to what amount and from whom? 3.Relief. Vide order dated 22.5.2014 the respondents No.1 and 2 were proceeded ex parte. Shri Amit Solanki appeared in the witness box as PW1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/1 reiterating the averments made in the claim petition. Copies of bills are collectively marked as Mark B. Copy of election card is Ex.PW1/L. Copy of certificate issued from Global Net India is Ex.PW1/M. 6. PW2 Shri Pankaj Gera, LDC in Sir Ganga Ram Hospital deposed that the petitioner Amit Solanki was admitted in their hospital on 01.02.2013. He had brought the original bills of Amit Solanki and the same are Ex.PW2/A (colly) wherein the details of the bills raised by the hospital and the payment made by the parents of the petitioner were given. It was stated by the learned counsel for the respondent No.3 that no RE was to be led. RE was closed on 22.5.2014. The petitioner was also examined on 22.5.2014 in terms of the judgment of the Amit Solanki Vs. Sumit Solanki Page no. 5 of 23 Hon'ble High Court on 11.1.2013 in MACA No.792/2006 titled Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Ranjit Pandey and Ors. 8. 10. The case of the petitioner is that on the night of 30/31st January, 2013 at about 3.00 a.m. the petitioner was coming back after attending a marriage function at Nangloi and the petitioner was accompanied by Shri Sumit Solanki who was driving the offending vehicle along with Shri Kuldeep Solanki and Shri Kaushal Kumar. It was averred that on the way at about 2/3 a.m. when the offending vehicle reached at Todarmal Road, Rattanpuri Chowk, the vehicle hit Amit Solanki Vs. Sumit Solanki Page no. 7 of 23 against a pole on the divider and the offending vehicle turned turtle and all the occupants received grievous injuries and became unconscious and the petitioner along with the other persons was removed to Lady Harding Hospital, New Delhi. It was stated that in respect of the accident FIR No.17/2013 under Sections 279/338 IPC was registered against the respondent No.1 at PS Inder Puri. In para 2 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/1 the petitioner had reiterated the mode and manner of the accident as stated in the claim petition. 11. The IO had filed Detailed Accident Report containing the criminal record consisting of copy of charge sheet; copy of tehrir, copy of FIR; copy of site plan; copy of DD; copy of MLC, copy of arrest memo and personal search memo, copy of seizure memos; copy of mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, copy of the notices under Section 133 MV Act, copy of verification report of the RC of the offending vehicle with the copy of the RC, copy of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle and its verification report and verification report of DL of the respondent No.1 with a copy of the DL, copy of school certificate of the respondent No.1, copy of order on application for release of the offending vehicle on superdari along with a copy of the superdarinama, copies of photographs and copies of duly verified bills in respect of Kuldeep Solanki. As per the FIR No.17/13 under sections 279/337 IPC, PS Inder Puri the case was registered on the basis of complaint of SI Sudesh Pal (on DD).
texts.arguments: As the petition has been filed U/s 166 M.V Act it was incumbent upon the petitioner to prove that he sustained injuries in an accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents/claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal (supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle Amit Solanki vs Sumit Solanki on 31 October, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119485754/ 3 of deceased. In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing the accident. The law Amit Solanki Vs. Sumit Solanki Page no. 10 of 23 is well settled that the compensation has to be awarded in personal injury cases under the following heads: (1) for loss of earnings during the period of treatment (2) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (3) expenses suffered by him on his treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food etc. However the petitioner would have incurred some expenses even subsequently. It has been held in Divisional Controller, K. S. R. T. C v Mahadeva Shetty and another AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4172 as under: 13."The damages for vehicular accidents are in the nature of compensation in money for loss of any kind caused to any person. In Parry V. Cleaver (1969 1 All. E. R. 555) Lord Morris stated as follows: "To compensate in money for pain and for the physical consequences is invariably difficult, but...... no other process can be devised than that of making monetary assessment." The case of the petitioner is that due to the accident on 31.1.2013 he received grievous injuries and became unconscious and he was removed to Lady Harding Hospital, New Delhi. It was averred that due to the accident the petitioner/injured suffered tremendous mental agony, pain, suffering and loss of earnings. It was stated in the charge sheet that as per the MLC of the petitioner the injuries were opined to be grievous. Thus the petitioner himself had stated that at the time of the accident he was not doing anything and as such it would be argued Amit Solanki Vs. Sumit Solanki Page no. 18 of 23 that there was no question of his suffering any loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident. The petitioner has also not produced any document to show that he remained on bed rest for any particular period and there is nothing to show that he was advised bed rest for any particular period or that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to work or to show the period for which he was not able to work. During examination by the Tribunal the petitioner had stated that at present he was not doing anything but there is nothing to show that the same was on account of the injuries sustained in the accident. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs. 25,000/ consolidated on account of loss of income.
